quotes.text: Teams is not an alternative stack. It's not demanding you replace the way you've always shipped code. It's simply another host for the app you've already built.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: The episode's central reframe for web developers.

quotes.text: If the myth is that you need to learn a new stack, the reality is you need only to adjust your setup, and that's a much smaller gap to cross
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Lowers the perceived barrier to Teams development.

quotes.text: When you run into login failures, don't fight the iframe. Switch to the SDK supported pop up flow. When routing acts unpredictable, drop server driven redirects, and stick with InApp navigation.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete troubleshooting guidance for auth and routing in Teams tabs.

quotes.text: By separating your core payload from the presentation, you give yourself flexibility down the road, no matter which Microsoft surface ends up consuming that data.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A durable API design principle for future Microsoft 365 hosts.

quotes.text: From a planning perspective, treat your team's integrations as public APIs version them so that future hosts don't break existing behavior.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear, actionable advice on versioning Teams integrations.

takeaways: Microsoft Teams is a host for your existing React, Node and Express app, not a new stack; the manifest, Teams Toolkit and Developer Portal handle the setup.
A personal tab runs your web app inside an iframe, so authentication needs the SDK-supported pop-up flow and navigation should stay client-side.
Designing message extension APIs with structured, versioned and presentation-free payloads prepares them for reuse in other Microsoft 365 surfaces such as Copilot.
hook: Many full-stack developers assume Teams development requires a whole new stack and give up at the setup screens. This episode is for React and Node developers who want their existing web apps inside Microsoft Teams. You will learn how to ship a personal tab, handle auth and routing quirks and design APIs ready for Copilot.
